title: Jensen Huang says he would return as Nvidia boss if asked by the board
summary: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.

blocks.text: Jensen Huang has said he would be "honored" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia, in his first public comments since his shock resignation after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.

In a statement shared with the BBC by a personal representative, Huang said: "I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely."
But he said he had had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia.
The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday.
The likelihood of Huang returning to the company is unclear, at best.
As the BBC reported on Monday, Nvidia's board was not looking to bring him back into the company.
The board is actively investigating his conduct, which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive.
Huang's affair with a woman suspected of being an asset for Beijing is set to see the billionaire questioned before multiple committees of US lawmakers in the weeks ahead.
